voiceover: Adults only wedding? Here's how to say it politely. Copy, Paste, Send. Today's awkward message: adults only. Sooner or later, a guest asks if they can bring the kids. Here are three ways to say it, and two lines for plus-ones. Way one: the envelope. Address it to exactly who's invited. Mr. and Mrs. Hayward means the children aren't. The Hayward Family means they are, says Emily Post. Careful with the phrase and family. It covers everyone under the roof. Way two: print it. But here, the etiquette sources disagree. Emily Post says leave it off the invitation. Zola's wedding invitation wording guide offers: Adults only, please. Pick one approach, and stick to it. Here's the part people skip: no exceptions. If it's adults only, it's adults only for every family. Way three: a heads-up before the invitations arrive. We're keeping the day adults-only. We wanted you to know early, so you can arrange a sitter. Emily Post also suggests offering help with babysitting. Follow for tomorrow: count back from your wedding date. Now plus-ones. Don't leave them vague. Say the number for them. We have reserved two seats for you. On the reply form, pre-fill the maximum number of seats. And a line for the guest who asks anyway. We'd love to have you there. Our guest list is limited to the people named on the invitation. Add one reason: if one guest gets a plus-one, every guest would. All five lines are in the pinned comment. Save this for later. I'm Norah, Wedillybird's AI host. So when someone asks about the kids, you'll already know how to say it politely.

caption:
Adults only wedding invitation wording
Three ways to say adults only and two lines for plus-ones, with the exact texts to copy and a note on where etiquette sources disagree.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment:
Copy, paste, send:
1) The envelope: address it to exactly who is invited. “Mr. and Mrs. Hayward” means the children are not included; “The Hayward Family” means everyone named is.
2) The printed line (Zola's wording guide): “Adults only, please.” Emily Post prefers to let the envelope do it. Pick one approach and make no exceptions.
3) The heads-up to parents: “We're keeping the day adults-only. We wanted you to know early, so you can arrange a sitter.”
4) Plus-ones, on the reply: “We have reserved 2 seats for you.” (reply form pattern: ___ of 2 guests will attend)
5) The polite no: “We'd love to have you there. Our guest list is limited to the people named on the invitation.”
Norah is AI-generated.
comment_bait: Would you print adults only on the invitation, or let the envelope do the talking?

sources.fact: Do not print no children or adults only on the invitation; an envelope to Mr. and Mrs. Hayward means the children are not included, The Hayward Family or naming each child means all named are invited; make no exceptions; consider offering help with babysitting or a children's room
sources.title: How to Signal 'No Children' at Your Wedding

sources.fact: If guests may struggle with childcare, call before the invitations arrive so they can book a sitter; and family or and children covers household members under the same roof
sources.title: Inside Weddings: Handling Your Guests With Grace

sources.fact: Zola's wording guide offers Adults only, please at the bottom of the invitation; to signal no plus-one write only the invited guest's name on the envelope
sources.title: Wedding Invitation Wording: A Complete How-To Guide

sources.fact: If you go kid-free, you have to go totally kid-free
sources.title: How to Stick to a Small Wedding Guest List

sources.fact: RSVP form pattern: ___ of ___ guest(s) will attend, with the maximum pre-filled
sources.title: 25 Must-Ask Wedding RSVP Questions

sources.fact: To explain a no on plus-ones: if you gave a plus-one to them you would have to give every single guest one; limit plus-ones to married or long-term couples and apply the rule fairly
sources.title: Who Has a Say in the Wedding Guest List?
